questions.hint: Read the three digits of \(809\) from left to right: the first digit is hundreds, the middle digit is tens, and the last digit is ones.

keyPoints.text: How is \(809\) written on the numeral expander
keyPoints.note: In a 3-digit number, the first digit on the left shows hundreds, the middle digit shows tens, and the last digit on the right shows ones.

questions.solution: \(809\) has \(8\) hundreds, \(0\) tens, and \(9\) ones.

steps.explain: Look at the first digit on the left of \(809\): the hundreds digit is \(8\) (highlighted in yellow).

questions.stem: Use the greater than (\(>\)) or less than (\(<\)) symbol to make the number sentence true. In a, which number sentence correctly compares \(45\) and \(63\)?

figure.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 340 92" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="65%" height="auto" style="max-width:442px;display:block;margin:0 auto;"><rect x="2" y="2" width="336" height="88" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="64" y="54" font-family="system-ui" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#0f172a">a</text><rect x="92" y="30" width="54" height="34" rx="4" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="119" y="52" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#0f172a">45</text><rect x="156" y="28" width="38" height="38" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="175" y="53" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui" font-size="16" font-weight="900" fill="#94a3b8">?</text><rect x="204" y="30" width="54" height="34" rx="4" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="231" y="52" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui" font-size="14" font-weight="800" fill="#0f172a">63</text></svg>

questions.hint: Compare the number of digits and the highest place-value digit of \(45\) and \(63\). The open end of the symbol always points to the larger number.

keyPoints.note: Compare the two numbers from the highest place value; the open mouth of > or < always faces the larger number.

questions.hint: Find ball \(6\) on the hill and see which valley (\(10\) or \(20\)) is at the bottom of its slope.

keyPoints.text: closest \(10\) that each ball would roll to
keyPoints.note: A ball on the hill rolls down the slope away from the peak (5, 15, or 25) into the nearest ten valley at the bottom of that slope.

questions.solution: Ball \(6\) sits on the slope going down to \(10\), so the closest \(10\) is \(10\).

questions.stem: Round each number to the nearest \(10\). Numbers that end with a \(5\) are rounded up. In a, what is \(19\) rounded to the nearest \(10\)?

questions.hint: Look at the ones digit of the number: if the ones digit is \(1, 2, 3,\) or \(4\), round down to the lower ten; if it is \(5, 6, 7, 8,\) or \(9\), round up to the next ten.

keyPoints.note: Check the ones digit: 4 or less rounds down to the lower multiple of 10, while 5 or more rounds up to the next multiple of 10.

questions.solution: \(19\) lies between \(10\) and \(20\). Since its ones digit is \(9\), \(19\) rounds to \(20\).

questions.stem: Round each number to the nearest \(10\). Numbers that end with a \(5\) are rounded up. In f, what is \(73\) rounded to the nearest \(10\)?

questions.hint: Look at the ones digit of the number: if the ones digit is \(1, 2, 3,\) or \(4\), round down to the lower ten; if it is \(5, 6, 7, 8,\) or \(9\), round up to the next ten.

keyPoints.note: Check the ones digit: 4 or less rounds down to the lower multiple of 10, while 5 or more rounds up to the next multiple of 10.

meta.question: 6j

questions.stem: Write some numbers and round them to the nearest \(10\). Which list shows all three numbers correctly rounded to the nearest \(10\)?
questions.hint: Check the ones digit of each number: \(5\) or more rounds up to the next \(10\), and \(4\) or less rounds down.

keyPoints.note: Check each number's ones digit: 5 or more rounds up to the next ten, and 4 or less rounds down to the lower ten.

questions.solution: \(45\) rounds up to \(50\), \(74\) rounds down to \(70\), and \(168\) rounds up to \(170\).

steps.explain: Check the first number \(45\): numbers ending in \(5\) round up to the next \(10\), so \(45 \rightarrow 50\).
Check the second number \(74\): its ones digit is \(4\) (less than \(5\)), so it rounds down to \(70\).
Check the third number \(168\): its ones digit is \(8\) (\(5\) or more), so it rounds up to \(170\).
Combine all three rounded results: \(45 \rightarrow 50,\; 74 \rightarrow 70,\; 168 \rightarrow 170\).
